section_title: Routes, navigation and shared application behavior
description: The signed-in area presents the following navigation order: Dashboard (/dashboard), Apply Leave (/apply-leave), My Requests (/my-requests), Leave Balance (/balance), Payslips (/payslips), Attendance (/attendance), Team Calendar (/calendar), Employees (/employees), Holidays (/holidays), My Assets (/my-assets), Reports (/reports), How It Works (/how-it-works).

section_title: Routes, navigation and shared application behavior
description: My Profile is reached through the account menu and opens /profile. Authentication and the login/sign-up/recovery views use /auth.

section_title: Routes, navigation and shared application behavior
description: Desktop has persistent navigation. A narrow viewport has a menu button that opens a navigation drawer with the same destinations, account identity, logo and Close button. The account summary includes avatar, full name and email. The account dropdown contains My Profile and Logout.

section_title: Routes, navigation and shared application behavior
description: Escape dismisses the account dropdown and then the drawer. The close button is also available. Route navigation was exercised throughout; the drawer sometimes remained open while a route changed and required closing. Do not assume that every navigation action auto-closes it.

section_title: Routes, navigation and shared application behavior
description: The shared header exposes a page title, Punch In shortcut, theme toggle and notification bell. The wide header also shows the description Leave Management System. The title on /profile remained Dashboard even though the page content was My Profile; this is recorded as an existing inconsistency, not a required behavior.

section_title: Routes, navigation and shared application behavior
description: Initial/full-page navigation can show a branded MOBIYANTRA splash and per-page loading content. Observed loading messages include Loading dashboard..., Loading your requests..., Loading leave balance..., Loading attendance..., Loading team calendar..., Loading employees... and Loading your assets.... Loaded content replaces those states.

section_title: Routes, navigation and shared application behavior
description: Initial sign-in showed a dismissible first-day welcome message with the user's first name and company. It stated that it would disappear in 30 seconds and provided an X. The eligibility rule for showing this message again, whether it depends on join date, and dismissal persistence were not tested.

section_title: Routes, navigation and shared application behavior
description: The UI exposes a Notifications alt+T region used for transient notifications/toasts. This region is distinct from the bell's notification history. The keyboard hint was visible in accessibility output; its actual shortcut was not exercised. Success/error toast wording for real submissions is unverified.

section_title: Routes, navigation and shared application behavior
description: Session timeout, session refresh, simultaneous sessions, logout behavior, unauthorized-route handling, deep-link restoration, offline handling and browser-back behavior during edited forms were not established. No access-control rule should be inferred from a menu item alone.
The header provides a reversible theme switch. In light mode its accessible title is Switch to dark mode; after activation it becomes Switch to light mode. The icon changes between moon and sun.

Toggling changes the portal's rendered backgrounds, cards, text and header treatment. Dark mode was seen on dashboard, forms, lists and attendance; it is a functional portal preference, not just a decorative icon.
Dark mode remained active after reloading the dashboard. It also appeared on several subsequent module visits. The exact persistence mechanism and lifetime were not inspected.

Authentication screens were light when opened separately while the employee portal had been dark. Later captures returned to light mode. No cause was established. Capture filenames containing dark describe the intended capture sequence, not proof of the actual theme; inspect each screenshot and the toggle title in its snapshot. The guide capture 41 was light.

Automatic system-theme detection, preference sharing across browsers/devices, first-visit default, auth-theme consistency and behavior after clearing browser data were not proven. The portal was left in light mode.

/auth presents Login and Sign Up tabs, with Login selected initially. The screen carries a company logo, the portal name and Leave Management System subtitle. Changing tabs does not require a different route.

Login has Email and Password fields, Forgot password? and a Login button. Email is type=email with placeholder your@email.com. Password is type=password with a masked-dot placeholder. Password text is concealed.

Neither login input exposed a native required attribute, minlength, maxlength or pattern in the captured markup. This only describes the rendered inputs; custom validation and server validation may still exist.
A real sign-in was completed by the user and reached the employee Dashboard. Credentials were not recorded in this documentation.

Invalid credentials, empty submission, blocked accounts, rate limits, login loading state, error wording, email normalization, redirects after login, password visibility controls and any MFA/email verification steps were not exercised. No SSO, remember-me or password-eye control was visible in the captured login view; this is not proof that no other auth flow exists.
Forgot password? replaces the tab content with a Forgot Password? view on /auth. It explains: Enter your registered email and we'll send you a reset link.

The view has Back to Login, Email Address and Send Reset Link. Email is type=email, required=true and placeholder your@email.com. Send Reset Link is a submit button. Back to Login returns to the login tab view.

No reset link was sent. Success wording, account-not-found handling, resend cooldown, reset-email content, link expiry, one-time use, the new-password screen, confirmation and post-reset session handling are unknown.

Sign Up is an alternate tab on /auth. The visible field order is Full Name, Email, Date of Birth, Join Date, Company, Department, Designation, Phone Number, Gender *, Role, Password and Confirm Password, then Sign Up.
Full Name: text input, John Doe placeholder, required=true. Email: type=email, your@email.com placeholder, required=true. Neither input exposed maxlength, minlength or pattern in the captured markup.

Date of Birth: native date input, required=true, max=2026-11-25 in this review session. That is the review date, indicating no future DOB is allowed by the current input constraint. No minimum DOB was exposed.
Join Date: native date input with no required, min or max attribute in the captured markup. Do not assume this proves server optionality.

Company: custom select with Select company placeholder and four choices: Wazirz Sm India Private Limited; Mobiyantra Private Limited; Riddlepay Private Limited; Finastraa Technologies Private Limited.

Department: Select department placeholder. Choices: Accounts, IT, Director, Office Boy, Management. The directory's filter contains only its four populated departments and does not include Director in this account's list.

Designation: Select designation placeholder. Choices: Accountant; Senior Accountant; Software Developer; Software Developer Intern; Accounts Intern; Office Boy; Director; Receptionist; Admin Executive; Web Designer. After selecting Mobiyantra Private Limited and IT, the designation menu still offered this full list. Department-based filtering was not demonstrated.

Phone Number: type=tel, placeholder 10-digit mobile number, required=true. No native pattern, minlength or maxlength was exposed. The placeholder expresses intended format; it does not prove digits-only or exact length enforcement.

Gender is visually marked with an asterisk and starts at Select gender. Choices: Male, Female, Other. The companion native select did not expose required=true, so actual custom validation is not established.

Role defaults to Employee. Opening the menu showed Employee as its only choice. There is no evidence of public HR/Admin self-registration from this form. This corrects the initial walkthrough's unverified role concern.

Password and Confirm Password are masked password inputs, both required=true. No native minlength, maxlength or pattern was exposed. Password strength, matching validation and error messages remain untested.

Company/department/designation/gender menus expose options through listbox/option semantics; choices can be selected and returned to the form. The values and displayed labels are preserved in JSON evidence.

Requiredness of custom company/department/designation controls, duplicate-email handling, phone validation, password requirements, sign-up loading/success/error states, account approval, invitations, terms, verification email, default permissions and automatic login are not proven. No account was created.

Dashboard has the current weekday/day/month, a greeting using the user's first name and a contextual salutation (Good Night observed), plus Here's your leave overview for today. The salutation schedule is unknown.
A monthly paid-leave usage indicator displays used/quota (0/1 in this account) with Used This Month and Paid Leave quota labels.

Summary cards are Monthly Quota (Paid Leave), Used This Month (Approved this month), Approved (Leave requests), Pending (Awaiting approval). They are distinct measures; pending requests are not shown as used. The snapshot alone does not establish all count/query rules.

Leave Balance shows Paid Leave days available and Permission Leave as Unlimited. Permission leave is described as available anytime, without quota deduction, but unpaid. Apply for Leave navigates to /apply-leave.
Recent Leave Requests has View all -> /my-requests. With no requests, it shows No leave requests yet and Apply for your first leave -> /apply-leave. A populated recent-request card was not available.

Number of recent items, default request sorting, request detail navigation and whether metrics update without a reload are unknown. The guide claims live balance/calendar updates; that is recorded separately.

Apply for Leave explains Submit your leave request and track its approval status. A balance notice shows Paid Leave availability and the one-day-per-month/carry-forward policy when balance data has loaded.

Leave Type is a required native select. Empty placeholder: Select leave type. Options: Paid Leave (1/month), value paid; Permission Leave (Unpaid), value permission. No other selectable type appeared in this form.

Selecting Paid Leave exposes a Paid Leave — 1/month quota card with Accrued Quota, Used and Remaining values and the carry-forward note. Current example: accrued 2 days, used 0, remaining 2. These are account data.

Selecting Permission Leave exposes an inline explanation that it is unpaid, has no quota deduction and has no frequency limit. Its side card says No quota tracking — this leave type is unpaid and not deducted from any balance. It does not present the paid-leave quota card as its own quota.

From Date and To Date are required native date inputs. Both had min=2026-11-25, the review date, and no exposed max. The captured form therefore prevents dates before that date through native minimum constraints. Whether the end-date minimum updates to the selected start date is unverified.
Reason is required, uses a multiline textarea and has the placeholder Please provide details for your leave request.... No native length constraint was exposed in the captured markup.

Attachment is optional. A Click to upload area advertises PDF, DOC, JPG or PNG with max. 5MB. The file input accept value is .pdf,.doc,.docx,.jpg,.jpeg,.png. Thus DOCX/JPEG variants are included in the actual picker constraint although the short helper text does not list them all. No multiple-file attribute was established by this record.

Submit Request and Reset are separate buttons. Reset was exercised: selected type, draft dates and draft reason returned to empty/default, and the type-specific quota card disappeared. No file was selected in this test.

Policy help says one paid day/month with carry-forward; Permission Leave anytime/unlimited/unpaid; weekends and company holidays do not count as leave days. The IT account specifically says Sat + Sun for IT.

The portal guide states that paid leave accrues monthly and carries forward indefinitely, never expires, and cannot be applied for a Monday or Friday. It says Permission Leave is the only leave type allowed on Monday or Friday. These exact restrictions were not proven by a submitted request.

Automated draft date entries did not reliably persist across field changes. The screenshots named Monday draft/date range do NOT prove Monday rejection, a valid range, or working-day calculation. No complete draft range or date-specific validation error was established. Preserve this as an inspection limitation rather than declaring a portal date-entry bug.

Exact working-day calculation; inclusive end date; zero-working-day ranges; cross-month/year treatment; paid-leave cap versus accrued balance; overlapping/past requests; minimum notice; partial days; insufficient balance; duplicate submission; pending-balance reservation; attachment size/type rejection, upload progress, remove/replace and download; network failure/retry; final submission confirmation and error copy are unknown.

section_title: Leave requests — search, filters, sorting and lifecycle
description: My Leave Requests shows a subtitle about tracking and managing requests and five counters: Total, Pending, Approved, Rejected, Cancelled. All were zero for this account.

section_title: Leave requests — search, filters, sorting and lifecycle
description: Search is a text input with Search by reason or leave type... placeholder. Draft search input was accepted; there was no populated request data to verify search matching, case sensitivity or debounce behavior.

section_title: Leave requests — search, filters, sorting and lifecycle
description: Filters toggles an expanded filter area. Status buttons: All, Pending, Approved, Rejected, Cancelled. Leave Type buttons: All, Paid Leave, Unpaid Leave, Work From Home. Status and type can be chosen together with search.

section_title: Leave requests — search, filters, sorting and lifecycle
description: Sort dropdown: Sort by Date (default, value date) and Sort by Status (value status). Selecting Sort by Status changed its displayed selection. Ordering direction/tie-breakers could not be tested without records.

section_title: Leave requests — search, filters, sorting and lifecycle
description: The list shows Showing N of M requests. With no results, it displays No requests found and suggests adjusting filters/search or applying for a new leave. The same empty message was seen with combined search/filters. No clear-all control was visible in the expanded filter area examined.

section_title: Leave requests — search, filters, sorting and lifecycle
description: Employee submission creates a Pending request and immediately alerts HR/Admin. There is a single approve/reject decision, with no multilevel approval chain described. Rejection can include an admin remark.

section_title: Leave requests — search, filters, sorting and lifecycle
description: Approval updates balance and team calendar, and the employee is notified. Status guide meanings: Pending = awaiting HR/Admin; Approved = accepted with balance/calendar updated; Rejected = declined with a remark if given; Cancelled = withdrawn following approved cancellation.

section_title: Leave requests — search, filters, sorting and lifecycle
description: Approved leave may be cancelled before it ends. The employee requests cancellation through My Requests; HR/Admin must approve it; the leave becomes Cancelled and balance is restored after cancellation approval.

section_title: Leave requests — search, filters, sorting and lifecycle
description: A populated request list/detail was unavailable. Record fields, status badges, request identifiers, per-record actions, attachment links, remarks display, pending-request withdrawal, editing, cancellation dialog/reason, cancellation rejection, intermediate statuses, history timestamps, pagination, notifications on cancellation and exact balance-reversal timing are unknown.

section_title: Leave requests — search, filters, sorting and lifecycle
description: The request filters expose Unpaid Leave and Work From Home, whereas the application form exposes Permission Leave and Paid Leave. These labels may reflect historic types, normalization or different rules; no equivalence should be silently assumed.
Leave Balance presents an overall percentage used, this month's quota, and this month's approved usage. Current values were 0% used, one-day monthly quota and zero approved usage.
Leave Quota by Type has a paid-leave card showing the one-day-per-month policy, Accrued, Used, Left and This month used/quota. The account's example was Accrued 2, Used 0, Left 2 and This month 0/1.
Month-wise Usage — 2026 is described as approved leaves taken each month. With no approved records it says No approved leaves taken this year yet. No year-selection control appeared in this view.
Policy text repeats Permission Leave's unlimited unpaid status, no balance deduction, and weekend/company-holiday exclusion.

The guide claims live balance updates and restoration after approved cancellation. Monthly accrual start date, partial-month proration, eligibility/probation, manual adjustments, negative balances, year-end rules, retroactive corrections and whether pending leave holds balance are unverified.

section_title: Attendance — current session, history and calculations
description: Attendance describes Track your daily punch in / punch out. There is a current-date panel, session heading, Punch In time, Punch Out time, Total Hours This Session and a primary Punch In action. The header has another Punch In shortcut. No live punch action was invoked during this review.

section_title: Attendance — current session, history and calculations
description: This account was in Session Complete state: current-day in/out times existed and a Punch In action was still available. This proves the control is displayed in that state; it does not prove a second session is allowed.

section_title: Attendance — current session, history and calculations
description: The session panel displayed 8.59 hrs for an example whose history displayed 8.6h, demonstrating different display precision. The panel uses AM/PM time presentation; correction inputs expose native 24-hour time values. Calculation/rounding policy and exact underlying timestamps were not inspected.

section_title: Attendance — current session, history and calculations
description: Four summaries appear: Present Days, Work From Home, Half Days and Avg. Hours/Day, each labelled Last 30 days. These are distinct metrics.

section_title: Attendance — current session, history and calculations
description: Attendance History has Refresh and a month selector. The captured choices were November 2026 through December 2025, in reverse order: Nov, Oct, Sep, Aug, Jul, Jun, May, Apr, Mar, Feb, Jan 2026, then Dec 2025. This is a 12-month displayed range; how it rolls forward is unverified.

section_title: Attendance — current session, history and calculations
description: History entries show weekday/day/month, attendance status, In, Out, Hrs and a pencil action titled Request correction. Entries were newest first in the observed months. Full Day was observed. Some Full Day rows had dashes for in, out and hours; status cannot be inferred from times alone.

section_title: Attendance — current session, history and calculations
description: Month changes fetch different history and affect the summary metrics. November showed 18 present / 7.2h average; October showed 20 present / 8.2h average; December 2025 showed 0 / 0h. The labels remained Last 30 days. This is a real labeling/data-scope ambiguity, not a rule to copy.

section_title: Attendance — current session, history and calculations
description: While a selected month's data loaded, Refresh became disabled; previous rows could remain briefly visible. The settled empty month showed No attendance records yet. Today's session panel remained visible while historical month selection changed.

section_title: Attendance — current session, history and calculations
description: Before-punch and active-session views, punch-out behavior, running timers, multiple sessions, breaks, overtime, shift assignment, lateness, half-day thresholds, overnight shifts, missed punch reconciliation, refresh completion feedback, location display in history and edit permissions are unknown.

The user explicitly confirms that punching in is location-based. This is part of required feature parity and must not be omitted because location controls are not visible on the idle attendance screen.

Idle/current-completed attendance views expose Punch In but did not show office coordinates, a map, allowed radius, accuracy, GPS status, work-site selector or location-permission help in the captured visible content.

It is not established whether the system merely records position, checks an office geofence, selects among office locations, uses browser GPS/IP, accepts remote work, or checks location again at punch-out. Do not equate the user's phrase location-based with a specific radius or algorithm.

Office coordinates, radius and units; company/site-specific rules; accuracy threshold; location freshness; low-accuracy handling; permission denied/blocked/unavailable/timeout states; outside-office messaging; user-confirmation step; retry; stored coordinates; visibility/retention; VPN/mock-location handling; HTTPS requirements and mobile browser behavior were not exposed by safe review.

Opening the live Punch In action might request location and immediately record attendance. It was therefore not used as an exploratory test. This is a documented inspection boundary, not evidence that any location check is absent. No GPS coordinates or permission grants were collected.

Preserve location-based punching in the build scope. Before implementing its exact rules, resolve the above decisions explicitly from business requirements rather than inventing them from screenshots. The record is usable without another portal visit, but it cannot establish hidden configuration that was never visible to this account.

Each examined attendance row has Request correction. It opens a Request Correction modal that states the request will be reviewed by the admin. The selected attendance date is displayed, not a separate date picker for choosing an unrelated day.
Fields: Corrected Punch In, Corrected Punch Out and Reason *. Times use native time inputs. Existing row times are prefilled (e.g. 10:08 and 18:43); a row with missing times opens with both empty.

Reason is a required textarea with e.g. Forgot to punch out placeholder. No native reason length constraint or time min/max was exposed. The time inputs did not have native required attributes in the captured markup.

Submit Request, Cancel and an X/Close control are present. With existing times prefilled, Submit Request was enabled even with an empty reason. With both times missing, it was disabled, including after a draft reason was entered. Exact enablement logic beyond these cases was not established.
Cancel closes the modal without saving. The parent page has My Correction Requests; this account shows No correction requests yet.

Whether one or both corrected times are required, end-before-start validation, overnight handling, allowed correction age, duplicate requests, approval status/details, admin remarks, cancellation, notifications, audit trail and effect on payroll/attendance totals are unknown. No correction was submitted and no status workflow was available to inspect.
Team Calendar is for viewing team availability and planning leave. It opens a month grid with month/year heading and previous/next arrows. The week begins Sunday and labels weekdays as S M T W T F S.

Day cells can display leave indicators and an overflow count such as +1. November 3 showed an overflow indicator; selecting it revealed a detail panel listing three employees on leave, with initials/name and leave type. The exact number of indicators shown before overflow was not established.

Selecting November 25 revealed its date heading and one team member on leave. The panel includes a close control. Selecting next month moved to December 2026 and removed the previous selected-day panel.
Clicking a December day with no recorded leave did not produce a new visible detail panel in the examined state. Do not assume a universal empty-day modal/message from this single interaction.

Leave-type legend: Paid Leave, Loss of Pay, Work From Home, Casual Leave, Sick Leave and Permission Leave. This exceeds the two application choices, so historic/display types and newly requestable types must be distinguished.

Below/alongside the grid: On Leave Today with team-member count and name/type list; Upcoming Leaves with Next scheduled leaves and empty message No upcoming leaves; Team Statistics with Total Team Size, On Leave Today, Upcoming Leaves and Availability Rate.

The review example had team size 31, one on leave and 97% availability. That is compatible with whole-percentage rounding of available/team, but the formula and eligibility scope were not proven. Today's summaries stayed present when the calendar moved to another month.

Which request statuses feed the calendar, date-span handling, half-day indicators, holiday/weekend markings, team/company visibility, upcoming window, ordering, per-person details, event pagination and automatic refresh cadence are unknown. The guide says approvals update the calendar live.

Employees shows Total, Working and Departments counts. The reviewed account had 31 total, 3 working and 4 departments. Counts are data, not fixed limits. They stayed at overall totals while filtering to Accounts.

Search placeholder: Search by name, email, designation.... Department selector defaults All; choices in this dataset: IT, Accounts, Office Boy and Management. Selecting Accounts reduced the visible list to that department.
List items show a sequence number, avatar or initials, full name, designation, department, and a status such as Working, Offline or On Leave. Sequence numbers restart in the filtered list.

Combining a department filter with a no-match search shows No employees found. Clicking one employee's name did not open a new page or detail panel in the tested state; do not invent an employee detail workflow.

Search matching/case/debounce, email visibility, status-calculation rules, real-time presence interval, sorting, pagination, directory visibility by company/role and avatar fallback specifics are unknown. Working status appears related to attendance but no rule was proven.
My Profile has Manage your personal information and account details text, avatar, role label, designation and department summary, and a Personal Information section.
Read-only presentation includes Full Name, Email, Phone, Gender, Company, Department, Designation, Date of Birth and Joined On. Dates are formatted as human-readable day/month-name/year values.
A pencil edit control switches the information section to an inline form. Editable fields: Full Name, Phone Number, Department, Designation, Date of Birth and Gender. Existing values are prefilled.
Edit placeholders: Your full name; +91 98765 43210; e.g. Engineering; e.g. Software Engineer. Department and Designation are free-text inputs here, despite being select controls at registration.

Profile DOB is a date input with max=review date and no native required/min. Gender select: Select gender, Male, Female, Other. No native required/length/pattern constraints were exposed on the editable profile fields.
Save Changes and Cancel are available. Cancel returns to the display view. Email, Company, Role and Joined On were not editable controls in the examined form. No save was performed.
The avatar is a Change profile photo button with camera affordance/Change text; its file input accepts image/*. No upload was performed.

Photo size limits, crop/preview/remove/default avatar, accepted MIME validation, upload progress/errors; profile save validation/errors; approval of employee-edited department/designation; whether identity changes propagate to all lists and historical records remain unverified.

section_title: Notifications — interface and observed event categories
description: The shared bell opens a Notifications panel anchored near the header. It lists a title, explanatory body and timestamp for each item. A bounded internal scroll region exposes older entries without scrolling the whole page. The bell toggles the panel closed again.

section_title: Notifications — interface and observed event categories
description: The history is displayed newest first in the examined list. Entries have small blue dot indicators. The meaning/read-state transition of those dots was not proven. Clicking a punch-out reminder did not navigate or produce a clear accessibility-tree change. No mark-all-read, clear-all, delete, notification settings or View all action was visible in the examined panel.

section_title: Notifications — interface and observed event categories
description: Punch-in reminder title: Haven't punched in yet? Body: Don't forget to mark your attendance for today. Examples were timestamped 11:00 am on November 9, 10 and 11.

section_title: Notifications — interface and observed event categories
description: Punch-out reminder title: Don't forget to punch out! Body: It's past 6:30 PM — please punch out before you leave for the day. Examples were timestamped 06:30 pm on multiple dates.

section_title: Notifications — interface and observed event categories
description: Birthday alert title: It's a birthday today! with a birthday emoji. The body names the employee and asks colleagues to wish them. Examined examples were timestamped 09:00 am. This demonstrates birthday notifications, not a proven universal schedule or audience rule.

section_title: Notifications — interface and observed event categories
description: Holiday Tomorrow alert with calendar emoji. Example body: Tomorrow is Diwali — the office will be closed. Example was November 7 at 06:00 pm for a November 8 closure. Recurrence rules were not independently tested.

section_title: Notifications — interface and observed event categories
description: New Holiday Added alert with calendar emoji. Body includes the holiday name, an ISO-format date and office-closed wording. The history contained examples for Diwali and Dussehra. Two identical Diwali-added entries had the same timestamp; duplicate handling must not be inferred from that data.

section_title: Notifications — interface and observed event categories
description: Displayed timestamps use abbreviated day/month and AM/PM, for example 25 Nov, 06:30 pm. No year appeared in those rows. Timezone and date rollover rules were not exposed.

section_title: Notifications — interface and observed event categories
description: Leave submission alerts HR/Admin immediately by email and WhatsApp and leaves the employee request Pending. The employee's access does not expose the recipient configuration or an actual HR notification inbox.

section_title: Notifications — interface and observed event categories
description: Leave approval/rejection decisions notify the employee by email, WhatsApp and in-app alert, while balance and calendar update. This is guide-described integration behavior, not independently verified delivery.

section_title: Notifications — interface and observed event categories
description: No evidence establishes payslip-publication, asset assignment, correction-decision, cancellation-decision, anniversary, payroll or other notification types. These must not be reported as existing features merely because they would be useful. Delivery channels for attendance/birthday/holiday alerts beyond the observed in-app list are also unverified.

section_title: Notifications — interface and observed event categories
description: Read/unread persistence, unread bell counts, deep links, push notifications, browser/OS permission prompts, polling/realtime transport, retention, pagination/infinite loading, preferences, quiet hours, resend/retry, failed delivery logs and template configuration were not exposed.

section_title: Notifications — office schedule confirmed by the user
description: Normal office hours are 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

section_title: Notifications — office schedule confirmed by the user
description: On working days, an employee who has not punched in by 11:00 AM receives a notification addressed to that person. The reminder time is one hour after the stated office start time. It is not a notification to every employee or to the whole company.

section_title: Notifications — office schedule confirmed by the user
description: At 6:30 PM, employees who have not punched out receive a notification. This is 30 minutes after the stated office end time. The user described it as the attendance reminder counterpart to the working-day rule.

section_title: Notifications — office schedule confirmed by the user
description: The user did not specify the office timezone, the exact working-day calendar source, approved-leave exemptions, whether someone absent all day receives a punch-out reminder, whether the check repeats, how multiple sessions are treated, or whether late/corrected punches suppress an already queued notification. No such detail should be silently invented.

section_title: Notifications — office schedule confirmed by the user
description: Preserve the confirmed targeted reminder behavior. The scheduler's eventual implementation must check the employee's attendance and working-day eligibility at the relevant trigger time. Defining timezone, holiday/weekend/approved-leave treatment and duplicate handling is a later business decision; it is not proof of the current scheduler's internals.

section_title: Notifications — office schedule confirmed by the user
description: Historical data has an ambiguity: the current holiday list marks November 9–11 as Office Closed, while the notification history contains 11:00 AM punch-in reminders on those dates. Historical calendar/configuration may have differed; the screen data does not establish why. The user's explicit working-day reminder rule takes priority for the replacement.

section_title: Holidays — fields and exact reviewed dataset
description: The route header says National Holidays; the content title is National Holiday Calendar with India Public & Gazetted Holidays subtitle. Holidays are grouped by month/year, with name, month/day, category and optional Office Closed designation. The reviewed list is for 2026.

section_title: Holidays — fields and exact reviewed dataset
description: Categories shown are National and Festival. A listed public holiday does not automatically carry an Office Closed badge. Do not treat every displayed national/festival date as an office closure without its policy flag.

section_title: Holidays — fields and exact reviewed dataset
description: No holiday search, year picker, employee editing or filtering control appeared in this employee view. Do not invent those controls as existing employee functionality.

section_title: Holidays — fields and exact reviewed dataset
description: Source of public-holiday data, annual updates, company and regional scoping, optional holidays, closures affecting balances, and editing permissions were not established. The guide says HR/Admin manages holidays.
Payslips describes View and download your monthly payslips. The account has No payslips available yet with the explanation that payslips appear once generated by HR/Admin.
The Admin Portal runs payroll and generates payslips. This implies an employee-facing published output, not a payroll generation control in the employee account.

Populated rows/cards, pay-month/year selectors, download format, preview, payslip fields, PDF layout, earning/deduction components, net pay, publication/revision, download authorization, taxes/contributions and publication notifications cannot be reconstructed from the empty state alone. No payroll formulas or jurisdictional rules are established by this record.
My Assets describes Company equipment currently assigned to you. The account shows No assets assigned to you yet.
The guide gives laptop, ID card and accessories as examples of company assets tracked here. They are examples, not a complete asset taxonomy.

Populated asset cards, identifier/serial, assigned date, condition, acknowledgements, return/repair requests, attachments, assignment history, employee actions, permissions and notifications were not exposed. No assignment/return management screen was visible to this employee account.

Reports & Analytics describes analyzing personal leave usage patterns and trends. Summary measures: Total Requests, Approved, Pending, Rejected. A Cancelled report counter was not present in this view, although it exists on My Requests.
With no request data the page says No leave data yet. Apply for leave to see your analytics. Leave Balance Overview still shows the paid balance remaining/total and monthly carry-forward note.
Export Report is present and disabled when the reviewed account has no leave data. No export file was generated.

Populated chart types, grouping, date filters, comparison periods, export format/columns, status scope, rounding and chart interactions are not exposed. This is employee leave reporting, not evidence of access to company-wide payroll/attendance reports.

A dedicated guide explains leave submission, attendance, payslips and other modules. Sections include Leave Request Journey, Leave Types Explained, Two Portals One System, Everything In The Portal, Request Status Guide and final get-started links.

Five-step leave journey: Apply for Leave; Instant Submission; Admin Review; You're Notified; Need to Cancel? It describes live balance checking, optional documents, email/WhatsApp alerts, single-step approval and restoration after approved cancellation. Detailed claims are preserved in sections 8–10/17.
Feature shortcut cards link to Apply Leave, My Requests, Leave Balance, Attendance & Punch, Team Calendar, Payslips and My Assets. Final CTAs link to Apply for Leave and Dashboard.

Employee Portal responsibilities: leave application/tracking, punch/attendance tracking, payslips/balance, team calendar/holidays. Admin Portal responsibilities: approve/reject leave, run payroll/generate payslips, manage employees, holidays and shifts. No additional admin screens were inspected.

Preserve the need for accurate user help and policy explanation in the replacement. The guide's exact graphic layout/copy is not a required design. Help must agree with the eventual confirmed business rules.

The replacement must work fully on mobile, tablet and desktop. This applies to authentication, forms, lists, calendar, notifications, drawers, account controls, dialogs, upload controls and all async states.

Explicit reference captures include 390px mobile dashboard and leave form, 768px tablet dashboard, 1440px desktop dashboard/leave form, and 1440px dark dashboard/attendance. Many other captures were taken at a 458px browser innerWidth with approximately 443px page content due to scrollbar measurement. Authentication re-review used 1280px browser innerWidth.

Navigation changes between persistent sidebar and drawer. Dashboard cards/forms reorganize at narrower widths. This proves the current portal has responsive treatments, not that every breakpoint or dialog is correct.

Exact breakpoints, all overflow cases, smallest devices, landscape, virtual keyboard, screen reader behavior, browser compatibility, reduced motion and all touch-target sizes were not comprehensively tested. Some narrow dashboard edges appear crowded/clipped. Do not copy those defects.

Feature parity includes usable keyboard/focus behavior, clear form labels, readable calendar/list data, notification scrolling, form validation feedback and loading/empty/error/success states across device sizes. These are completion requirements for the new build, not retrospective claims that all of them worked in the current portal.

Employee identity is reused by account menu, profile, greeting, directory, calendar and notifications. Registration/profile expose company, department, designation, role and personal details as distinct concepts. The storage schema and cross-company access rules are not visible.

Leave application, balance, requests, dashboard, calendar and reports are connected concepts. Accrued, used, remaining, monthly usage and request counts must remain distinct. The guide connects approved cancellation to balance restoration; the exact transaction model is unverified.

Current attendance session, daily history, correction requests, directory presence and scheduled reminders are related features. Their internal event processing and status-calculation rules are unknown.

Holidays carry a category and closure designation. Working days depend at least on the department weekend policy shown for IT and company holiday policy text. The confirmed reminders require a working-day decision.

Proposed implementation entities can be derived later, but this inspection does not prove table names, APIs, database vendor, backend framework, realtime provider, messaging vendor or existing source architecture. No hidden application state, storage, credentials or source code was inspected.
